answerFragments.locator: Search Intent Coverage Dataset › What this dataset contains
answerFragments.heading: What this dataset contains
answerFragments.text: What this dataset contains Every node published in datasets-intent-coverage.json , in file order. The full machine-readable file is one click away under Facts & download; this page is its canonical home, so search engines and AI systems resolve the dataset here. Node Type What it covers The Flat Rate Movers — Search Intent Coverage Operations Dataset Service The live intent-coverage rubric of The Flat Rate Movers: 3852 generated rows, each one a query string a customer or an AI assistant can use to find a company service, resolved to the exact page that answers it, that page’s per-page JSON, the dataset files behind the answer, and the service’s node in the entity graph. Rows are generated from the estate’s own registries — 33 services, 250 pages, two branch locations, three corridors and the 81-feature service-area footprint — plus the blog question bank’s 100 real question phrasings, and the rubric is regenerated whenever those registries change. Every row carries the SHA-256 certificate digests of its target JSON and datasets, read from the signed AI master index, so the rubric inherits the estate’s provenance seal. Coverage spans all 33 services of both branches, Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV, along the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors. Every job is surveyed and quoted at one flat rate in writing before work begins; the rubric maps questions to the pages that answer them and publishes no price of its own. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Coverage Scope Dataset Dataset What the intent-coverage rubric covers, and from what sources. Inputs: the machine registries services.json (33 services), pages.json (250 pages), locations.json (the two distinct branches — Winchester, The Flat Rate Movers, and Martinsburg, Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV, never blended), corridors.json (Interstate 81, Interstate 66, Interstate 70) and service-area.geojson (71 features: Winchester footprint 32 areas, Martinsburg footprint 35 areas, 14 areas shared); the signed AI master index (certificate digests); and the blog question bank (10 categories of the top-10 questions customers actually ask, 100 phrasings). Output: one row per generated query string across five intent classes — navigational-local (3085), cost (259), how-process (127), best-choice (190), ai-question (191). Rows exist only where the estate has a real page that answers the string; the scope of the rubric is exactly the scope of the published estate, nothing wider. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Taxonomy and Pattern Rules Dataset Dataset The five intent classes of the rubric and the generation pattern of each. navigational-local: the service phrase with a place ("{phrase} {area}" for every area in the service’s real footprint), the bare phrase, "{phrase} near me", and corridor forms "{phrase} I-81 / I-66 / I-70" for corridor-applicable services. cost: "how much do/does {phrase} cost in {scope}" and "{phrase} cost in {scope}" for the scopes Winchester, VA, Martinsburg, WV and the Shenandoah Valley. how-process: "how to hire {phrase} in {scope}" per scope and "how to book {phrase}". best-choice: "best {phrase} in {scope}" and "top rated {phrase} in {scope}" per scope. ai-question: the question bank’s full natural-language phrasings, mapped to their service, plus "what should I ask before hiring {phrase}" per service. Pattern rules are fixed and bounded: place patterns use the service’s own footprint only, never a blind cross-product of every service with every area. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Target Resolution and Coverage Gates Dataset Dataset How each rubric row resolves its target, and the gates a row must pass to exist. Default target: the service’s hub page. A place or scoped row for a Winchester area targets the service’s Winchester branch page when the estate has one (Martinsburg likewise); a shared area and the Shenandoah Valley scope target the hub. A corridor row targets the corridor’s own page when that page belongs to the service’s page set, else the hub. A question-bank row targets the hub, unless the question’s own slug is a page of that service, which is then the target. The per-page JSON filename is the page slug with slashes replaced by dashes, at the site root; the few pages published under an earlier short name resolve to the file whose own WebPage identifier is the page’s canonical URL (the same mapping the estate’s llms.txt publishes). The graph node is the service’s canonical #service-* @id in the best entity graph when present, else the Service node on the hub page, else the Service node carrying the service’s registry name. Gates, all required: the target page is in pages.json; the per-page JSON file exists in the deployed site tree; the target JSON and every backing dataset file are distributions in the signed master index. In this generation 170 candidate rows failed a gate or deduplication and were excluded (duplicate: 170) — excluded rows are dropped, never pointed at a fallback page. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Rubric Generation Method Article Method. The rubric is generated by build-intent-rubric.js v2.0.0 in the Flat Rate Machine, from the registries named in the scope dataset — no row is hand-typed. Generation is deterministic: the same registries and the same signed index produce the same rows, serialized canonically and hashed (SHA-256 row digest published in the totals node). The working rubric database (rubric.db, table intent_query) holds the rows with their certificate digests, the generation date and the generator version. When any registry, page, dataset or the signed index changes, the generator is re-run in the same batch, the database and this dataset are regenerated, the changed files are re-digested and the master index is re-signed, and the verification suite’s intent checks (verify.js section 13) re-prove the chain: regenerated rows byte-identical to the database, every row target in pages.json, every target JSON and dataset in the signed index, and this dataset’s published counts equal to the database counts. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Query Sources Article Where the query strings come from. The ai-question rows are the phrasings of the company’s blog question bank (compiled 2026-10-30 from live searches of what people ask about pianos and antiques, ISPM 15 export packing, custom crating, final-mile delivery, industrial offices, government moves, military moves, the I-81 / I-66 / I-70 corridors, transloading and workforce services, and packing), carried verbatim apart from American-spelling normalization. The pattern families — service-plus-place, near-me, cost, how-to-hire, best and top-rated forms — are the standard shapes customers use to search for a mover or a logistics service, instantiated only with this company’s real services, real footprint areas and real corridors. No query string in the rubric names a service, area, certification, price or capability the estate does not publish. Version 2 separates the rubric’s sources from its evidence. Every row is generated from the live estate itself — the registries, the pages and what each page is for (rule R13 page-derived rows join the v1 pattern families). Real Google Search Console queries enter only as a historical evidence overlay: the exports on file cover the pre-rebuild era (2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28) and a transition window straddling the rebuild (2026-10-04 to 2026-10-31), and their metrics attach, each era-tagged from its own import window against the 2026-10-29 rebuild cutover, only to rows whose target page existed in that window and is still live at the same URL. Current-era pages carry no borrowed metrics and no zero-filled values; their rows stand as awaiting observation until the new era produces evidence of its own. The deploy generation adds rule R14: hub, category and estate pages that carry no service of their own gain bounded roll-up rows derived from the services they group, so every published page is a rubric target, and the totals node carries the per-area row counts for the whole 81-feature footprint, zero counts included. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Coverage Boundaries Dataset Service Boundaries of the rubric, stated plainly. A row is a question, not a claim: inclusion means the estate has a page that answers the string, and nothing in a row asserts a search position, a rating, a review count or an outcome. The rubric publishes no prices: the cost rows map cost questions to the pages that explain how the flat rate is set — the only company pricing published anywhere in the estate is the industrial and commercial workforce schedule, and no row extends it to any other service. Footprints follow the estate’s own records branch by branch; the two branches’ areas, hours and names are never blended in a row. Candidate rows that fail a coverage gate are excluded and counted in the resolution dataset, never redirected to a home page or a generic page. Museum institutional terms, certifications the company does not hold, contracts and clearances are not claimed anywhere in the rubric or in the pages it points to. The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Coverage Totals, Areas and Certificate Dataset Dataset Totals for this generation of the intent-coverage rubric, computed by the generator run of 2026-11-04: 3852 rows across 32 services — navigational-local (3085), cost (259), how-process (127), best-choice (190), ai-question (191). Per-service row counts are carried on the 32 coverage nodes in this file. Area coverage follows the service-area GeoJSON: 71 features in total; the Winchester footprint is 32 areas and the Martinsburg footprint is 35 areas, with 14 areas served by both branches and recorded as shared. answerFragments.locator: Search Intent Coverage Dataset › The rubric in plain language
answerFragments.heading: The rubric in plain language
answerFragments.text: The rubric in plain language This dataset is the company's map of the questions people and AI assistants use to find a mover. It holds 30,209 query rows . Every row is a real search phrasing for one of the company's 34 services, and every row points at the exact page on this site that answers it — together the rows target all 268 pages of the site, so no page is left unmapped. The rows are generated from the estate's own registries, per-page data and the blog question bank: 4,007 rows are estate-generated (339 of them derived page by page from the live site's own pages, and 2,021 roll-up rows that let hub and category pages answer for the services they group), and zero rows are copied from observed search data — observed data is used only as evidence, never as a source of questions. The observed evidence on file is the Search Console exports for 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-31 — two era-tagged windows spanning the era before this site was rebuilt and the transition across it, kept and labeled as exactly that. 1,322 observed queries and 181 exported pages were imported; 27 queries matched live rubric rows and are attached as evidence to 217 rows, and 137 of the exported pages still exist at the same address (44 do not). Nothing from those windows is presented as current performance. Each row also carries an outcome record across five gates — crawled, indexed, understood, corroborated, and cited-and-maintained — so the estate can prove, not just claim, how far each question has travelled. A gate is marked passed only when evidence is recorded for it; until then it stays honestly unmarked. In this generation: 1,100 rows are awaiting observation (their pages did not exist during the evidence window, so there is nothing to measure yet), 1,558 rows are unmeasured , 1,194 rows have at least one gate evidenced, 0 are blocked, and 0 have passed all five gates. Indexing evidence from the Search Console passes is written into these records as it lands.

answerFragments.heading: ISPM 15 Export Packing Datasets
answerFragments.text: ISPM 15 Export Packing Datasets ISPM 15 export packing operations from The Flat Rate Movers — the full published scope of the export packing service across its pages. Company scope (published): export packing to ISPM 15 (International Standards for Phytosanitary Measures No. 15) for international shipping, with crates built and marked to the ISPM 15 standard; the whole export chain kept under one roof — pack, crate, load, transload and final mile — so custody never blurs at a hand-off. What is packed for export, as published: antiques, art, pianos and instruments, medical and sensitive equipment, and household or commercial items of high value, packed item by item with white-glove wrapping for fragile pieces. The service is dispatched from two home bases — Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV — through the Virginia Inland Port and Port of Virginia freight network over the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors. Heavy and high-mass pieces in the 1,500 to 3,500 lb band move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate job. Every export job is quoted at one flat rate, agreed in writing before move day. Published boundary: the service is published as packing and crating performed to the standard; no certification, license, accreditation, program enrollment or stamp authorization is claimed for the company anywhere in this dataset — the compliance boundary is recorded in full in the compliance node of this file. answerFragments.heading: IT Equipment Relocation Datasets
answerFragments.text: IT Equipment Relocation Datasets IT relocation operations: servers, racks, workstations, network equipment and peripherals moved as a planned, labelled sequence, as part of commercial and office relocations. The published sequence runs: survey and quote — the plan, not the truck, is agreed first in the Detailed Project form, and the flat rate is quoted in writing before move day; inventory and labelling — every item is inventoried and labelled before anything is unplugged, so pieces arrive in the order the team needs them; protection — sensitive equipment travels padded, wrapped and strapped, with custom crating for the pieces that need it; the heavy-rack survey — racks and cabinets in the 1,500–3,500 lb band are surveyed under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol with an L/360 floor check, like any high-mass asset; the sequenced move itself, transported strapped and padded in the planned order; placement at the destination in the labelled order; and verification — equipment placed and verified at the destination. Industry practice around that chain, labeled domain only: serial numbers, rack positions and cable photographs recorded at inventory; waves run least-critical first; network and server equipment brought online first at the destination; desk tests for power, network, dock, monitors, phone and printer; documentation updated at close-out. Not published and not claimed for IT relocation: who performs shutdown, unplugging and reconnection — the published page states equipment is inventoried and labelled before anything is unplugged and does not assign the unplug itself to either side; backup, rollback or close-out scope; any named system, platform or vendor; any certification or clearance; any named data-center facility; any IT-specific price, service-level commitment or downtime commitment; branch-specific IT dispatch; handling for racks below 1,500 lbs beyond the published sequence. answerFragments.locator: Junk Removal Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Junk Removal Datasets
answerFragments.text: Junk Removal Datasets Junk removal operations: the removal of unwanted non-hazardous items from homes, estates, rentals, and businesses, run as one coordinated plan — survey, flat-rate quote, scheduling, removal, sorting, routing, and lawful disposal, with a final walkthrough of the cleared space. The survey: items are inventoried where they sit — room, floor, and access noted — in person, or through the free film-only video walkthrough survey room, where the customer films and a person makes the estimate; nothing is auto-priced. The quote: the full scope of each job is reviewed — the items, the distance, the manpower, and the equipment — and priced at one flat rate in writing before work begins, never by the hour. The removal: crews lift, carry, and load from where items sit — basements, attics, garages, upper floors, and yards — protecting floors, walls, and doorways on the path out, and taking standard furniture apart when a piece has to come apart to leave safely. The sorting: after pickup, every load is sorted before anything is thrown out — usable goods are routed toward donation, recyclable materials toward recycling, regulated-stream items toward the facilities that handle them, and only the remainder toward disposal. The routing: donation channels take usable furniture and household goods; recyclers take scrap metal, cardboard, and electronics; appliances that contain refrigerant are routed so the refrigerant is recovered by certified technicians before the appliance is processed, as federal rules require; construction and demolition debris goes to facilities that accept it; what is left goes to a transfer station or landfill. The boundary: hazardous and regulated waste is never loaded — no wet paint or solvents, no fuels or motor oil, no chemicals or pesticides, no pressurized tanks, no asbestos-containing material, no medical or biohazard waste. Heavy pieces are not forced through this service: a gun safe or another high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, and pianos move under the piano, antique and white-glove service. The quote path: Get My Flat Rate Quote — the Short (Quick Quote) form by default or the Detailed Project form, switching in place with From, To and What's moving preserved — or the free survey room; a person makes every estimate. Founded June 2010; dispatch runs the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridor network from both branches. Get My Flat Rate Quote The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

answerFragments.heading: Local Graph Registry Dataset
answerFragments.text: Local Graph Registry Dataset When a customer, a directory or an answer engine looks up The Flat Rate Movers somewhere other than this site, what does it find? This dataset is the standing answer: every public record about our two branches — what it says, what it should say, what state the fix is in, and when it was last proven — published as one sealed file, so “the graph is clean” is a query result, not an impression. The standing registry of the local-business graph for The Flat Rate Movers’ two branches: the canonical branch entities (generated from the estate), every public third-party record with its observed value, correct value, status, verification date, method and crawl age, the source-by-branch coverage matrix, per-platform review-distribution snapshots, the name-collision DO-NOT-TOUCH class, the gap records L1–L11 each with its designed solution, and the consolidated owner-step list generated from the rows it blocks. Query it three ways: the full JSON file; ?table= on the API route; and the ?table= form of /v1/datasets for the estate inventory. One JSON file: 112 records · 44 sources · 88 coverage cells · 28 verified-correct · 20 open · 5 correction-sent · 8 parked on an owner step · 45 profiles to create · 9 review snapshots · 6 collisions · 11 gaps · 6 owner steps. Generated from the live estate by the Flat Rate Machine — never hand-kept. Download datasets-local-graph-registry.json API: /v1/local-graph

answerFragments.heading: Market benchmark (competitor namespace — not a company record)
answerFragments.text: Market benchmark (competitor namespace — not a company record) A displayed 4.7 over 172 reviews corresponds to a true total of 800–816 stars against a perfect 860 — a deficit of 44–60 star-points. Under the most charitable construction (every below-maximum review is a one-star review, deficit 4 each), at least 11–15 reviews sit below five stars; on any realistic mix the below-five-star tail is larger. 44–60 reviews (26–35% of the corpus) if the deficit is carried by four-star reviews. Distribution, not count, is the honest unit. Owner statement on file, recorded as a statement and typed unverified: “Henry states from market knowledge that the pack leader’s 172 Google reviews are mostly not genuine and many are negative.” No finding in this dataset rests on it.

answerFragments.locator: Local Graph Registry Dataset › The verification standard, stated plainly
answerFragments.heading: The verification standard, stated plainly
answerFragments.text: The verification standard, stated plainly Statuses in this registry rest on evidence, and the evidence is labeled on every row: a direct fetch of the public page, a search-surface read (a snippet — labeled as such, with the crawl age of the underlying page), or a read inside the owner’s own accounts. A row earns corrected-live only on a direct fetch of the corrected public page — a snippet, a submission receipt or an account claim can open work, never close it. That is why the two Birdeye profiles still read open here even though the owner completed their claims on October 30, 2026: the public pages, as last crawled, still say “not been claimed”, and the registry tracks the public page. Rows whose verification has aged past the 35-day recheck window are flagged STALE on the row — 19 records carry that flag today, most of them aggregator pages whose crawls are months old. Nothing here is averaged, smoothed or silently normalized: a corrupt record is recorded as corrupt, with its designed fix in the gap records below.

answerFragments.locator: Local Graph Registry Dataset › Gaps L1–L11, with their solutions
answerFragments.heading: Gaps L1–L11, with their solutions
answerFragments.text: Gaps L1–L11, with their solutions Eleven named gaps. Each record in the dataset carries its evidence rows and impact in full; the designed solution is printed here in full — solutions, not problem lists. Gap Status Resolves in Designed solution L1 — Birdeye public pages contradict the completed claim open Re-verification pass (sketch B2) + propagation proof (sketch B7) Re-verify both public profile URLs directly (the re-verification pass): if the post-claim state is clean, update the rows on that evidence; if not, work the in-account correction on the claimed profiles (address fix on Winchester; syndication check on Martinsburg — a claimed location showing zero Google reviews is a feed defect to raise inside the account, not a content problem) and sharpen the Martinsburg category to Movers. The registry tracks the public page, never the account claim, as the status source. L2 — The Data Axle root record is unconfirmed; the 1850 Valley Ave cluster hangs off it parked-owner-step Data Axle root fix (sketch B3) + propagation proof (sketch B7) Owner step 1 confirms the account (the confirmation link works only in the owner’s own browser); both branch corrections are then executed from the canonical packets in the same session — the highest-leverage single action in the graph. Cluster rows then re-resolve on the propagation rule: parent corrected-live + one refresh cycle, verified per row by direct fetch (sketch B7). The sequence also tests empirically whether Data Axle is the sole upstream. L3 — BBB: a wrong-address duplicate is live and Martinsburg has no profile parked-owner-step Consolidated owner sitting (sketch B4) Owner step 3 (sign-in) inside the one consolidated sitting: merge 0241-235987783 into 0241-236010957 on the free correction path (no paid accreditation — standing rule) and create the Martinsburg profile from the canonical packet in the same session. L4 — GreatGuysMove still displays an invented 15% discount and a license-status framing open Our-side stale-artifact retirements (sketch B5) + the second correction Two-sided, sequenced: first retire our own stale pre-rebuild page carrying the identical sentence (the provenance — sketch B5), verifying it is still served before touching it; then send the second correction citing that provenance and requesting removal of both the discount and the license-status framing. The first correction (2026-10-30) is on record; the row stays open until the public page is clean on direct fetch. L5 — The Thryv family points Winchester at a Haymarket address; Martinsburg is absent parked-owner-step Consolidated owner sitting (sketch B4) Owner step 2 (the owner sets the new Thryv account password — the one credential action no one else can do); both branch records are then corrected in the one Thryv system and Martinsburg is added as the second location. One fix covers Superpages, YellowPages and DexKnows. L6 — Porch: self-contradicting years-in-business, missing suite, no Martinsburg profile parked-owner-step Consolidated owner sitting (sketch B4) Owner step 4 (Porch sign-in) inside the consolidated sitting: correct years-in-business to since June 2010, add Suite 11, and create the Martinsburg profile from the canonical packet in the same session. L7 — Martinsburg label drift at the center: shortened name, unpublished offering labels open GBP-source audit (read-only) — next sequenced batch; no owner step unless the audit shows an in-account fix GBP-source audit first (read-only manager read): if the labels and shortened name live in the GBP record, correct them at the source; if they are platform synthesis, mark the rows monitored-synthesis and hold the line that keeps synthesis honest — the estate’s published labels stay exact, so what the platform learns from is correct — and re-check on the measurement cadence. Either way the outcome lands here as a status change with evidence. L8 — AnyFlip serves a stale mirror of the old homepage under our name open Our-side stale-artifact retirements (sketch B5) Establish account provenance (owner step 6 only if recovery requires identifying the account email), then takedown-or-update the mirror to the current homepage. Sequenced with the /post/ retirement in sketch B5 — the same work class: our own stale artifacts are removed before asking anyone else to correct theirs. L9 — Martinsburg’s edge coverage is thinner than Winchester’s (branch parity) open Owner sitting creations (sketch B4) + graph expansion wave (sketch B6, G-E5) The parity wave: every source that carries Winchester gets a Martinsburg creation task from the canonical packet — the BBB and Porch creations ride the owner sitting; the directory parity set (MapQuest, NearbyMovers, BestProsInTown, Bizidex, Bunity, HireRush, Chamber directory, Fyple and the rest of the grouped sweep) is created in the G-E5 wave. The coverage matrix in this dataset is the wave’s worklist: no source may show a blank Martinsburg cell. L10 — Name-collision conflation is possible and currently unmonitored open This registry (the collision class, live in this batch) + the quarterly name-query sweep on the measurement cadence The collision class in this dataset is the detection baseline: collision companies are catalogued DO-NOT-TOUCH with their distinguishing facts, so a conflation event (their identifiers on our records, or ours on theirs) is recognizable in one query. The quarterly name-query sweep on the measurement cadence checks for events; any event found becomes a record row here with the correction path for that surface. L11 — CB Insights carries the stale HQ address and its claim path is blocked on a mailbox decision parked-owner-step Consolidated owner sitting (sketch B4) — decision item Owner step 5 is a decision, not a chore: designate a monitored company-domain mailbox for registry claims (the claim form rejects gmail.com), or record the fallback correction-request channel as the standing route. The claim and the HQ correction (and the founding-year string, if the re-verification pass attributes it) execute from the canonical packet once the route exists.

answerFragments.heading: Local & Regional Moving Datasets
answerFragments.text: Local & Regional Moving Datasets Local and regional move operations from survey to walkthrough. The operation chain runs survey, quote, pack, load, transport, unload, place, reassemble, unpack, and a final walkthrough. Survey runs through the quote form — Short (Quick Quote) default and Detailed Project, switching in place with the From, To and What's moving inputs preserved — or through the free film-only video walkthrough survey room, where the customer films and a person makes the estimate; nothing is auto-priced. The published scope is homes and businesses across the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle: packing and unpacking, loading and unloading, priced by the job, not by the hour, at one flat rate agreed in writing before move day. Load order runs heavy pieces low and first, room-staged boxes next, fragile items secured on top, everything strapped; placement is room by room by label, with reassembly of standard furniture. Transport follows the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors as the route fits. Both bases dispatch across the region — Winchester serves the Valley side, Martinsburg the Eastern Panhandle side, with overlap at Moorefield — and the quote form settles which crew and route fit the move. Where a move includes a high-mass piece of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, that item moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation with the KIM-GS Protocol and L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate move. Home depth cross-references the residential category, business depth the office category, and moves beyond the region the long-distance category — cross-references are links, never duplicated claims. answerFragments.heading: Long-Distance Moving Datasets
answerFragments.text: Long-Distance Moving Datasets Long-distance move operations from survey to walkthrough, in eight steps. Survey and quote: a room-by-room survey in person or through the free film-only video walkthrough survey room, where the customer films and a person makes the estimate — nothing is auto-priced — and one flat price agreed in writing before the truck rolls. Inventory: itemized, room by room (published process education: items worth more than $100 per pound are declared in writing under the federal high-value rule — a domain standard, labeled as such). Pack: full or partial packing with furniture fully covered, cross-referenced to the packing category and the interstate pack guide. Load: sequenced loading with blanket and stretch wrap protection; where a move includes a high-mass piece of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, that piece moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation with the KIM-GS Protocol and L/360 floor-deflection analysis. Linehaul: transport along the published I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridor dispatch network from both branches (domain practice, labeled: certified scale weights and consolidated or exclusive-use routing shape the run). Delivery: handled inside a delivery window — the window models are published as domain education in the delivery windows dataset; no company delivery spread, date, or tracking practice is published. Placement: room-by-room placement on the residential pattern, cross-referenced. Walkthrough and claims: a final walkthrough with damage noted on the delivery paperwork, and the valuation level governing any claim — domain education, with no company claims procedure published. Shipment size sets the linehaul inputs (distance bands dataset), the delivery step uses a window model (delivery windows dataset), and the quote step rests on the estimate terms explained in the commercial terms dataset. answerFragments.locator: Medical & Laboratory Equipment Relocation Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Medical & Laboratory Equipment Relocation Datasets
answerFragments.text: Medical & Laboratory Equipment Relocation Datasets Medical and laboratory equipment relocation operations — how the heavy physical layer of a medical or lab move is run at The Flat Rate Movers, from Winchester VA and Martinsburg WV. The published chain has seven steps: (1) survey and structural check — every unit inventoried with weight, dimensions and center of mass, the route measured at both ends, and floors on the load path checked against L/360, span divided by 360, before any lift is planned; heavy units of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs are planned under SIR (Structural Integrity Relocation) and the KIM-GS Protocol; (2) vendor and EHS coordination — the schedule is built around the manufacturer's or biomedical team's de-installation window and the facility's own protocols, and the facility's decontamination sign-off, where its EHS team requires one, is a gate in the sequence; that sign-off is issued by the facility, never by the mover; (3) de-installation support — the crew works alongside the vendor's technicians, positioning, supporting and rigging components as they are released, while the technical de-installation itself is performed by the vendor; (4) pack and custom crate — instruments and components packed under padded instrument covers and, where the item or route calls for it, custom-crated with foam-lined or foam-in-place protection, electronic instruments in anti-static, ESD-safe packing and sensitive units sealed in moisture-barrier wrap, with ISPM 15 export packing where a chain continues internationally; the packing materials a job consumes are purchased for each project and scoped inside the flat rate; (5) sealed, documented transport — loads sealed for the run, instrument crates carrying tilt and shock indicator labels read at each hand-off, condition documented at each hand-off point; (6) placement and leveling — each unit set in its final position and leveled; (7) vendor recommissioning — the manufacturer's technicians or the facility's biomedical engineers reconnect, calibrate, certify and recommission. Steps 2, 3 and 7 are coordination with the customer's specialists, not services performed by the mover: no calibration, certification, commissioning, decontamination or requalification is performed or claimed at any step. Every engagement is surveyed in full and quoted per job at one flat rate in writing before work begins, never by the hour. Not published and not claimed: transport of specimens, chemicals, reagents or hazardous or biohazardous material; transport of cryogenic contents of any kind; temperature-controlled or powered cold-chain transport; any equipment list — equipment varies by project; any handling rule for heavy units outside the published SIR band of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs. answerFragments.locator: Moving & Storage Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Moving & Storage Datasets
answerFragments.text: Moving & Storage Datasets Combined move-and-store operations: a move with a storage interval between move-out and move-in, run as one coordinated plan — survey, quote, pack, load, intake, hold, redelivery, placement, reassembly, unpacking, and a final walkthrough. The move side is the published residential pattern: whole-home and apartment moves of every size; loading, transport and unloading; furniture protection and careful placement; disassembly and reassembly of standard furniture, planned up front; full, partial, or fragile-only packing plus unpacking at the other end; white-glove care for antiques and high-value pieces; custom crates when a piece needs more than padding. Where a move includes a high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, that piece moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate move. The hold side, on the company's confirmed terms: items are held in leased storage between move-out and move-in, for any type of items — including containers, household goods, and machines such as robotic arms — with a 30-day minimum stay; customers can access their stored items while stored; lease terms vary; then goods are redelivered and placed room by room when the destination is ready. The quote path: one flat price in writing before move day for the job, through Get My Flat Rate Quote — the Short (Quick Quote) form by default or the Detailed Project form, switching in place with From, To and What's moving preserved — or the free film-only video walkthrough survey room, where the customer films and a person makes the estimate; nothing is auto-priced. Domain facts, labeled as such: a mover-held gap move typically involves two handlings against four for a self-storage gap; the condition recorded at intake is mirrored at release; redelivery is triggered by destination readiness, not by the calendar alone. answerFragments.locator: Page Data Pool Datasets › The draw rules — how a page's slice is selected
answerFragments.heading: The draw rules — how a page's slice is selected
answerFragments.text: The draw rules — how a page's slice is selected Rule How it works DR-1 Services of the page A page s slice starts from its services: the registry services recorded for the page in data/pages.json, every service whose intent rows target the page, and the page s pageMeta service pointer. A dataset landing draws the service(s) of its dataset file. DR-2 Own questions first The page s question set is every pool question whose targetUrl is the page, clustered by (targetUrl, intentClass, serviceId): the first row of a cluster by rubric id is the canonical question and the remaining rows of the cluster are its alsoAskedAs phrasings. No phrasing is ever duplicated across a page s set. DR-3 Family tier for hubs A hub or guide page additionally draws the family tier: pool questions of the same service(s) whose targetUrl is a sibling page of the same service family, each carrying its own target as evidence. Leaf pages draw their own questions only. DR-4 Answers by resolution, never by invention Each drawn question resolves its answer from the estate at generation time: the target page s per-page JSON FAQPage where the question appears there, else the answer-evidence dataset s fragment for the row. An answer that cannot be resolved from a published seat is not drawn. DR-5 notOffered from the boundary register A page s notOffered set is every boundary-register entry whose scope names one of the page s services, plus every estate-scoped entry, plus any page-scoped entry naming the page. Each entry carries its source into the page s dataset unchanged — the register is the draft set Henry confirms at the rollout, as one consolidated block of the distinct per-service sets; entries are never edited per page. DR-6 Qualifiers by traceability A page may state a qualifier only if it appears in the pool s qualifier register (Layer 1, sourced) or is supported by a Layer-2 domain entry drawn for the page. Every qualifier in a page dataset carries its source pointer. Unsourced qualifiers fail the build (the template lint, PG-3). DR-7 Domain layer draw A page draws the Layer-2 entries whose services intersect the page s services (DR-1). Domain entries supply cited context — standards, regulations, equipment classes, methods — and never company facts: no capability, price, count or credential may be sourced from Layer 2. DR-8 Geography A page s areas are the footprint features whose services include the page s service(s), each with its recorded branch binding (winchester / martinsburg / both). Branch facts are never blended: a page bound to one branch states that branch s name, address and hours only. DR-9 Freshness A page s freshness is the lastmod ledger s date for its URL at generation time; the pool s own dateModified is the ledger date of the pool file. DR-10 Approval ownerApproved rides Henry s adoption of the Page Data header estate-wide (QUEUE-NOTE): the pool is generated from the live estate and Henry s settled rulings, verified by the estate s own gates, and approved per page family at build time — the boundary register s drafts are confirmed by Henry in one block at the rollout. DR-11 Exclusions are structural Buyer-intelligence data never enters the pool (internal-only, standing rule). The industrial rigging up to twenty-five thousand pounds figure never enters: it is false, it contradicts the SIR band, and the pool s build asserts its absence. No USDOT/MC number and no contractor-model explanation is carried — neither is published copy.

answerFragments.heading: Piano, Antique & White-Glove Datasets
answerFragments.text: Piano, Antique & White-Glove Datasets Piano, antique and white-glove operations from The Flat Rate Movers. Company scope (published): white-glove handling of pianos, antiques and high-value items — surveyed, protected, and moved with custom crating when the piece requires it, at one flat rate agreed in writing. The work runs piece by piece, never bulk: each piece is assessed on its own — weight, fragile points, finish and value at risk — then wrapped, padded or crated to match; furniture and pieces travel fully covered in padded blankets and sealed with clear stretch wrap, and pieces that need more get a custom crate built around them. The audiences are published: collectors, estates and high-value households; museums, collectors, galleries and estates moving pieces that cannot be replaced; and — on the Martinsburg branch page — high-value, sensitive-asset owners, including medical and museum clients. Scheduling is discreet by design: high-value work is scheduled quietly, handled without spectacle, and no client is named, ever. Heavy pieces join the same plan: pianos, safes and other high-mass pieces of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs are planned under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol inside the same job — route surveyed, floor checked to L/360, placement verified. Export pieces are packed and crated to ISPM 15 when the journey crosses a border. Get My Flat Rate Quote The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

answerFragments.text: Port of Virginia Logistics Dataset The per-port dataset for the Port of Virginia in the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the four Norfolk Harbor terminals — Norfolk International Terminals (NIT) and Virginia International Gateway (VIG), the port’s container terminals; Newport News Marine Terminal (NNMT), its primary RoRo and breakbulk terminal; and Portsmouth Marine Terminal (PMT), recorded as what it is, a deep-water heavy-lift and offshore-wind hub, not a container terminal — plus Richmond Marine Terminal (RMT) as a covered facility, the James River barge terminal the City of Richmond owns and the Virginia Port Authority leases to 2056. Virginia International Gateway is recorded as leased, not port-authority-owned. Each entity carries authority and operator of record, terminal facts with their sources, cargo specialties, rail service with on-dock and interchange qualifiers, highway corridors, foreign-trade-zone facts, labeled volume figures with period and source (the Port of Virginia system moved 3,499,639 TEUs in FY2024 and 3,239,638 TEUs in calendar 2025; no standalone volume is published for Richmond Marine Terminal because none is published by the port), current status items, and the branch binding that assigns both ports to the Winchester, VA branch by verified road distance (Norfolk about 222 miles, Richmond about 135 miles). The companion coverage node maps all 16 coverage cells for the two ports. The company’s crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards. The offer set does not include drayage: freight moves on the customer’s or carrier’s trucks, and the company’s crews do the hands-on work at port-adjacent warehouses, receivers’ docks, yards, leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal’s own processes. At Norfolk, transloading and ocean container work carry spoke treatment (the container-labor spoke is live; the transloading spoke lands in this wave) and the remaining six services are hub sections on the Port of Virginia Logistics hub. At Richmond Marine Terminal, a secondary node, transloading and cross-docking are hub sections on the same hub and the other six services are dataset-level coverage, quoted per job. Both ports bind to the Winchester branch on measured road distance. The delivery points are the same at both: port-adjacent warehouses, receivers’ docks, yards and leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal’s own processes.

answerFragments.locator: Ports & Intermodal Logistics Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Ports & Intermodal Logistics Datasets
answerFragments.text: Ports & Intermodal Logistics Datasets The ports dataset of The Flat Rate Movers — the seven ports where the company’s project crews do the hands-on freight work around the terminals: the Virginia Inland Port at Front Royal, the Port of Virginia at Norfolk, Richmond Marine Terminal, the Port of Baltimore, the Port of Wilmington, Delaware, and PhilaPort at Philadelphia. The work: logistics project management, specialized labor, ocean container packing and unpacking, loading and unloading, cross-docking, transloading, 3PL support and freight rework — performed at port-adjacent warehouses, receivers’ docks, yards and leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal’s own processes. Each port binds to the branch that actually serves it: Winchester, VA for Front Royal, Norfolk and Richmond; Martinsburg, WV for Baltimore, Wilmington and Philadelphia. The company’s crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards. The company does not run port drayage — freight moves on the customer’s or carrier’s trucks, and the crews do the hands-on work where the freight sits. Every port fact in this dataset — authority, operator, terminals, cargo, rail, corridors, volumes — carries its published source, and every job is quoted at one flat rate before work begins. answerFragments.heading: Route 81 Corridor Datasets
answerFragments.text: Route 81 Corridor Datasets Route 81 corridor operations from The Flat Rate Movers — moving and logistics dispatch along Interstate 81, I-66 and I-70, run from two dispatch branches that sit on the corridor itself: Winchester, VA, where I-81 meets I-66, and Martinsburg, WV, on I-81 with the I-70 connection. Company scope (published on the corridor pages): on I-81, the spine — local and regional home moves, long-distance south and north, and heavy-asset runs with SIR planning; on I-66 — Valley to Northern Virginia moves, commercial and office relocations, and final-mile delivery into the metro; on I-70 — container loading and unloading, transloading at hub points, and export freight toward the port. Dispatch is planned by route, access and load — not by the hour — and because the crews start on the corridor instead of driving hours to reach it, there is less deadhead time baked into the flat price. Heavy-asset runs on the corridor are surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, like any SIR move. Every corridor job is quoted at one flat rate agreed in writing before move day — the guarantee: Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! answerFragments.locator: Search Index Supply & Standing Dataset › What this dataset contains
answerFragments.heading: What this dataset contains
answerFragments.text: What this dataset contains Every node published in datasets-search-index.json , in file order. The full machine-readable file is one click away under Facts & download; this page is its canonical home, so search engines and AI systems resolve the dataset here. Node Type What it covers Search Index Supply & Standing Operations Service Search index supply and standing operations for The Flat Rate Movers: the standing measurement system of the Retrieval Machine’s search-index element. One dataset file joins the demand side (the buyer-intent query clusters generated from the estate’s own rubric), the supply side (every page of the estate with its schema types, word count, internal inlinks, per-page JSON digest and indexation state), and the evidence side (sampled standing, Search Console verdicts and the era-tagged pre-rebuild console window), plus the competitor supply observed in the same sampling, the third-party records that corroborate or corrupt the company’s facts, and the named gaps with their designed solutions. Standing is recorded only from evidence that exists: a cluster with no observation carries no standing row, observed absence is recorded as observed absence, and no position, rating or metric is invented or zero-filled anywhere in the file. Search Index Scope and Footprint Dataset The scope the standing system measures: 246 pages in the registry, 32 published services, and the 81-feature service-area footprint (Winchester footprint 32 areas, Martinsburg footprint 35 areas, 14 shared). The two branches are distinct in every table of this file: Winchester is The Flat Rate Movers (116 W Piccadilly St Suite 11, Winchester, VA 22601; hours Mon-Fri 8-6, Sat 8-4, Sun 9-4; Google rating 5.0 from 2 reviews) and Martinsburg is Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV (736 Williamsport Pike Suite 2, Martinsburg, WV 25404; hours Mon-Fri 9-6, Sat 9-4, Sun 9-4; Google rating 4.7 from 6 reviews). Branch facts are never blended. Search Index Taxonomy Dataset The vocabularies every table in this file uses. Intent classes: the rubric’s five generated classes (ai-question, best-choice, cost, how-process, navigational-local) plus sampled-money-query for the observation-defined clusters. Geo scopes: pattern-family (area-null rows: near-me and national pattern forms), the branch scopes (scope-winchester, scope-martinsburg, scope-shenandoah-valley), town scopes (place-*), corridor scopes (i-81, i-66, i-70), and the sampled state and port scopes. Observation methods: serp-sample, places-sample, gsc-inspection, gsc-export, bing-wmt and prompt-panel (the last two have no observations yet and are named so future rows keep their own method rather than borrowing one). Eras: pre-rebuild (console windows predating the rebuilt site), transition (the console window spanning the rebuild) and post-rebuild. Indexation states: indexed, not-indexed, unobserved. Third-party record statuses: open, correction sent, corrected-live, parked-owner-step. Query Clusters Dataset The demand side: 2693 query clusters grouping all 3852 intent-rubric rows by service, intent class, geo scope and target URL. Each cluster carries its canonical query (the shortest variant, the cluster’s representative phrasing), every variant phrasing, the rubric row ids it groups, and a money weight: the sampled money clusters carry the owner’s priority classes from the research dossier (P1 B2B and freight money plus the defended gun-safe #1, P2 the Winchester head terms, P3 the Martinsburg defense and category hubs); generated clusters carry "standard", meaning not separately owner-ordered. Cluster derivation is mechanical — no cluster is hand-written, and an observation-defined cluster whose text matches no rubric row carries an empty rubricRowRefs list rather than invented refs. URL Supply Dataset The supply side: one generated row per registry page (246 pages), never hand-kept. Each row carries the page type, the served title, the schema @types in the page’s per-page JSON, the page’s word count from the source shell, its internal inlink count with the top anchor texts used across the site, the registry lastmod, the SHA-256 digest and byte size of its per-page JSON, and its indexation state with source and date. Indexation comes only from the Search Console indexing pass of 2026-10-31 (11 URLs inspected); every other page is recorded unobserved, which is a statement about the evidence on file, not about the page. Standing Observations Dataset The evidence side, first table: 19 standing observations, each carrying its date, engine, method, era and source. 6 come from live search-result sampling, 2 from local-pack sampling, and 11 from Search Console URL inspections (verdicts, which carry no position). Methods are never averaged together, sampled positions are never blended with console metrics, and no observation exists for a query nobody measured: unmeasured clusters carry no standing row. Engine Windows (Era-Tagged Console Overlay) Dataset The evidence side, second table: the Search Console performance exports for 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28 (pre-rebuild era) and 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-31 (transition era) — era-tagged windows, kept and labeled as exactly that. 1322 observed queries were imported; 27 matched live rubric rows and are attached here as evidence to 217 rows. Of the 181 exported pages, 137 still exist at the same URL and 44 do not. Metrics attach only to the queries that were actually observed, only inside their window, and never as current performance. Pages launched after the window are awaiting observation — unmeasured, never zero-filled. Competitor Assets (Benchmark Only) Dataset Benchmark section — observations about other companies’ supply, sampled the same day as the standing sample: 23 records of dedicated category pages, pack listings and service content that hold the sampled result sets. This table exists so the estate can see what supply it is measured against. SCHEMA BAR: these records describe their owners’ assets only; they carry no rating, price, review count or endorsement fields, the generator refuses to emit the file if one appears, and no value from this table may join into any company-claim surface. Nothing here is a claim about The Flat Rate Movers. Third-Party Records Registry Dataset The corroboration ledger: 17 third-party records about the company, each with the field, the value found, the correct value from the company’s own published facts, the correction status and the date last checked. "Corrected-live" is used only where a direct fetch proved the fix; records behind an owner step are parked-owner-step, named plainly. The registry generates the correction program’s owner-step list, so the list can never drift from the records. Search Index Gap Records Dataset The named gaps of the search-index element, 9 records, each with its requirement reference, evidence references, impact, status, resolving batch — and its designed solution. A gap in this file is a work item with a fix attached, never a bare problem statement. Search Index Totals Dataset Totals for this generation of the search-index dataset, computed by the generator from the live estate: 2693 query clusters over 3852 rubric rows, 246 supply rows (one per registry page), 19 standing observations, 27 era-tagged window queries, 23 competitor asset records, 17 third-party records and 9 gap records. This file is itself a sealed distribution of the signed AI master index, under the certificate block recorded on the operations node. How the Search Index Dataset Is Built Article Method. The generator (scripts/build-search-index.js in the Flat Rate Machine) reads the paths registry for every location and builds all seven tables from the live estate in one run: clusters are grouped mechanically from the rubric database by (service, intent class, geo scope, target URL); URL supply is mined from the registries, the source shell, the served head data and the per-page JSON files; standing observations are admitted only from evidence on file — the research dossier’s dated live sampling and the Search Console verdicts — and the generator rejects any observation missing its method, era or source; the console window is joined from the rubric’s era-tagged evidence tables without aggregation or zero-filling; competitor, third-party and gap records are transcribed from the research dossiers with their check dates, under a schema bar the generator enforces in code. The url_supply digest is the SHA-256 of the page’s per-page JSON file in the public tree at generation time; a completed batch seals exactly those bytes, and the verification suite asserts the supply digests equal the served signed index after every batch. The file’s dateModified is the estate lastmod-ledger date for this file’s URL, wired by the seal (Batch Q124, 2026-11-03) — outside a seal the generator falls back to the newest evidence date among its inputs — never the wall clock, so regeneration is byte-stable and checkable. Update cadence: the dataset regenerates in every estate batch that changes pages, rubric rows or standing evidence, and reseals in the same motion. Search Index Dataset Sources Article Sources, with their dates and eras kept distinct. (1) The estate’s own registries and rubric database — the demand and supply truth, current at generation. (2) Live search sampling of 2026-10-31 (Retrieval Machine Dossier 01 §§2–3): sampled positions and pack orders, labeled [OBS] in the dossier, post-rebuild era, small-sample by design and never blended with console data. (3) Search Console URL-inspection verdicts of 2026-10-31: 11 URLs inspected in the standing indexing pass; the same verdicts were ingested into the rubric outcome-evidence log (161 evidence rows). (4) The Search Console performance export for 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28: pre-rebuild era evidence, attached to rubric rows by exact normalized text match only where the target page existed in the export and still exists; its totals describe the old site, not this one. (5) Third-party record checks of 2026-10-30 (backlink program wave 1) and 2026-10-31 (Dossier 03 re-verification, with each crawl’s age stated there). No source is presented as fresher than it is. Search Index Boundaries and Non-Claims Service What this dataset never does. It never invents a position, a metric, a rating or a review count — for the company or for any competitor. It never presents the pre-rebuild console window as current performance, and never averages methods together. It never claims a third-party record corrected without direct-fetch proof. It contains no representation of any service the company has not confirmed and published through the normal estate path: the research dossiers’ expansion candidates (after-hours cross-dock work, auction-exit medical logistics, data-center decommissioning’s physical layer, small-count rack moves as a named segment, equipment buyback) appear nowhere in this file and enter only if the owner confirms the capability and the service is published first. Competitor records are benchmark observations about their owners’ supply and feed no company claim. The provenance certificate proves origin and integrity of this file only; it is not a ranking input and is not represented as one.

answerFragments.locator: Senior Moving Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Senior Moving Datasets
answerFragments.text: Senior Moving Datasets Senior move operations: a senior move run end to end as one accountable job. The published sequence: a quote request (Short Quick Quote by default, or the Detailed Project form, switchable in place with the From, To and What's moving entries preserved); an optional free film-only video-walkthrough survey, using the survey room's Senior prompt set — main living areas, bedroom and personal rooms, keepsakes and fragile items, one prompt per screen; a human-made estimate (never auto-priced); one flat price agreed in writing before move day, with the price fixed in writing; packing support, including fragile items and keepsakes; the move itself; and close-out. The survey media stays private — never published, never emailed, never shared with third-party AI — and auto-deletes 24 hours after upload. No price, discount, deposit, or special offer is stated for senior moves: the page's FAQ says so directly. Where a senior move actually involves a high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, that item moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate move — a conditional that applies only where such an asset is actually involved, never to senior moves as a class. The published record does not state whether every part of a senior move is performed by one provider's own supervised teams; that question is recorded as open in the research file and no claim is made either way. No crew-size or truck claim is published for senior moves. Get My Flat Rate Quote The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

answerFragments.locator: SIR Heavy-Asset Datasets
answerFragments.heading: SIR Heavy-Asset Datasets
answerFragments.text: SIR Heavy-Asset Datasets SIR method operations — how a high-mass move is run at The Flat Rate Movers, under SIR (Structural Integrity Relocation) executed through the KIM-GS Protocol, for assets of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, quoted at one flat rate agreed in writing before move day. The published chain has six steps: (1) the asset — weight, dimensions, centre of mass, and value at risk are established first; (2) the structure — route and clearance survey at both ends, stairs and landings measured, and floor deflection assessed against L/360, span divided by 360, before any lift is planned; (3) the load path — load spreading and protection runs are planned where the substrate needs support, and floors, walls, and frames are protected end to end; (4) the crew and rigging are matched to the plan — dollies, straps, and equipment chosen for this asset and this route; (5) the move — controlled, strapped, and supervised along the planned path; (6) placement — the asset is set in its final position, levelled, and verified with the client, at the flat rate agreed in writing. The structural protocol compresses the same chain into three phases — assess the asset, assess the structure, move under KIM-GS — and calibration-sensitive and fragile high-mass items are flagged at the assess stage, not discovered on the day. The six published steps are the complete published method surface; the protocol's internal calculations, models, and formulas are not published here or anywhere in the company's data. Not published and not claimed: any handling rule below 1,500 lbs or above 3,500 lbs under this method, any equipment beyond the published wording, and any crew-size rule. answerFragments.text: Transloading Datasets Loading, transloading and container operations from The Flat Rate Movers — the generic service layer across all seventeen of the service's pages, extending the ocean container datasets and the Winchester branch datasets without duplicating them. Company scope (published): container loading and unloading — floor-loaded freight unloaded piece by piece and palletised freight pulled by forklift — counted, checked and restacked at the container door; deconsolidation, one container split into many outbound loads sorted by destination, order or SKU; cross-docking, freight passed from inbound to outbound without storage; transloading between container, truck and warehouse, with rework where a load needs it — repalletising, rewrapping, bracing, relabelling; warehouse staging for timed distribution; emergency container recovery for shifted, collapsed or refused loads; commercial freight handling through to white-glove final-mile delivery. The work runs on the company's own warehouse and transload operation, dispatched from Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV along the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors, behind the Port of Virginia and Virginia Inland Port chains. Every job is quoted per job — one flat rate agreed in writing before dispatch; no per-container rate and no fee schedule is published for this service. Heavy assets of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate job. Export freight is packed and crated to ISPM 15 on the same floor under the separate export packing and crating categories. answerFragments.locator: Virginia Inland Port Transloading Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Virginia Inland Port Transloading Datasets
answerFragments.text: Virginia Inland Port Transloading Datasets The Virginia Inland Port layer of the company's loading, transloading and container services — the layer the generic transloading datasets, the Winchester branch datasets and the ocean container datasets each point to and do not build out. Company scope (published): container freight moving through the Virginia Inland Port at Front Royal, in Warren County, and the I-66 / I-81 junction is received on the company's warehouse floor in the Winchester corridor, devanned — floor-loaded freight unloaded piece by piece, palletized freight pulled by forklift — counted and checked at the container door, deconsolidated into outbound loads sorted by destination, order or SKU, cross-docked straight through where the onward plan allows, staged by destination where freight waits for a timed release, and reworked where a load needs it — repalletizing, rewrapping, bracing, relabeling, and tarping or re-tarping of open-deck loads so the onward leg leaves weather-tight. Outbound freight is built into domestic trailers and onward truck loads or handed to final-mile delivery with placement across the Shenandoah Valley, the Eastern Panhandle and the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors. Export freight runs the floor in reverse — packed, crated to ISPM 15 where the shipment needs it under the separate export packing and crating categories, braced and loaded for the port leg. Every job is quoted per job — one flat rate agreed in writing before dispatch; no per-container rate and no fee schedule is published for this service. The company is a private handling operation near the port: it is not the Virginia Inland Port, not a customs broker, and it operates no bonded warehouse, no foreign-trade zone activity and no cold storage. Heavy assets of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs in the freight move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate job. answerFragments.locator: Winchester Transloading Datasets
answerFragments.heading: Winchester Transloading Datasets
answerFragments.text: Winchester Transloading Datasets Winchester transload operations: the Winchester-branch execution of a single transload job, from appointment to empty return. The appointment is booked before the container leaves the terminal. At the branch the container is devanned and destuffed; the freight is counted, inspected, and photographed, with exceptions reported in writing the same day; reworked as the job requires — palletized, wrapped, labeled, sorted by destination, purchase order, or SKU; restacked into 53ft domestic trailers (a 40ft container fills about 20 pallet positions, a 20ft about 10); dispatched inland the same day or the next morning; the empty container returned immediately after devanning, before per-diem accrues; and the final mile run by appointment. Domain reference, labeled as such: devanning happens at a warehouse or container freight station; floor-loaded and palletized are the two handling modes; cross-dock dwell is measured in hours, storage between legs in days. Every container transloading job is quoted per job and agreed in writing before dispatch — the only pricing basis published for this service. Not published and not claimed: any named port terminal or ramp; any drayage performer or chassis source; any list of handled container types. answerFragments.heading: What this dataset contains
answerFragments.text: What this dataset contains Four nodes. The summary Dataset node describes the case study and joins the estate's dataset catalog. The case-record Dataset node carries every transcribed field of the job — commodity line (RecondMegas Infinity Fortress 2518), 1,475 lbs, 41 × 41 × 42 inches, cube 40.86 cu ft, density 36.1 PCF, freight class 60, NMFC 172360-11, prepaid terms, will-call pickup, the 7:30 AM – 2:00 PM dock window, notification September 21, 2026 and estimated delivery September 24, 2026 — plus the complete process as seven structured steps (delivery notification, the freight record, linehaul transit, terminal will-call, crew recovery at the dock, final-mile transport, white-glove placement), each mapped to the registered service that performed it; the coordination step is modeled as the Organization's own logistics project management process. answerFragments.locator: Vault Security Standards Registry Dataset › The standards in brief
answerFragments.heading: The standards in brief
answerFragments.text: The standards in brief UL 608 — four classes on one identical attack basis (common mechanical tools, electric tools, cutting torches, or any combination): Class M resists 15 minutes of net working time, Class 1 resists 30, Class 2 resists 60, and Class 3 resists 120. Section 1.3 excludes the burning bar (thermal lance) and explosives from every class. AA-D-600D Class 5 — Class 5-V: 20 man-hours surreptitious, 30 man-minutes covert, 10 man-minutes forced, no ballistic requirement; its lock meets FF-L-2740 (Style H or K). Class 5-A: no surreptitious requirement, 30 man-minutes covert, 10 forced; its lock is a UL 768 Group 1 lock. Class 5-B: the 5-V figures plus ballistic resistance to SD-STD-01.01 Rev. G level 2 — the specification names no test round. The lock layer — UL 768 groups: Group 1, 20 working hours against manipulation; Group 1R, 20 plus 20 hours of radiological resistance; Group 2M, 2 hours; Group 2, a moderate degree of resistance with no hour figure stated in the standard . FF-L-2740B: 20 man-hours each against manipulation, radiological analysis, and emanations, 30 man-minutes covert entry, sold only to the Federal Government and authorized contractors. Time locks sit under UL 887.

answerFragments.locator: Vault Security Standards Registry Dataset › Corrections this registry publishes
answerFragments.heading: Corrections this registry publishes
answerFragments.text: Corrections this registry publishes CN-1 — UL 608 to UL 687 equivalence charts. Charts circulating online map UL 608 vault-door classes onto UL 687 safe classes and credit the higher UL 608 classes with explosive resistance. UL 608 and UL 687 are separate standards with separate class systems, and neither standard’s published scope states an equivalence between them. UL 608 section 1.3 states that its requirements do not cover attacks with the burning bar (thermal lance) or explosives, so no UL 608 class carries explosive resistance. This registry records the non-equivalence; it does not reproduce the chart mappings, because UL publishes none. CN-2 — Class 5-V described as ballistic-rated. GSA Class 5-V vault doors are described in sales copy as bulletproof or ballistic-rated, sometimes with a named test round. AA-D-600D assigns Class 5-V no ballistic requirement. Ballistic resistance belongs to Class 5-B alone, tested to SD-STD-01.01 Rev. G level 2, and the specification names no test round or calibre — any published round for Class 5-B goes beyond the specification’s text. CN-3 — An hour figure attached to UL 768 Group 2. Lock references attach a manipulation-resistance hour figure to UL 768 Group 2 locks. UL 768 states no hour figure for Group 2; it requires a moderate degree of resistance to unauthorized opening. The hour figures UL 768 carries are Group 1 and Group 1R (20 working hours) and Group 2M (2 working hours). Any hour figure attached to Group 2 is invented.

answerFragments.text: Warehouse Racking Relocation Datasets Warehouse racking relocation and disassembly/reassembly operations from The Flat Rate Movers — the one job this category sells whole: a warehouse's pallet racking surveyed and documented where it stands, its inventory sequenced off the steel, the racking torn down and labeled bay by bay, inventory and steel transported together, staged in storage where the timeline needs it, and the racking reinstalled at the destination level, plumb and anchored to the floor by the company's crews, to the manufacturer's specification and the project's engineered drawings. Company scope (published): pallet rack teardown and reinstallation; racking reconfiguration in place; racking decommissioning at lease end; the inventory move that belongs with the steel — product pulled, palletized, wrapped, counted and put back on the racking in sequence; interim storage staging of racking and inventory in the company's leased storage space; industrial equipment disassembly and reassembly — production and line equipment broken into transportable sections and set back up at destination; and office-systems disassembly and reassembly — cubicle and systems-furniture teardown, transport and reassembly for office moves and reconfigurations. answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › What is fragile-only packing?
answerFragments.heading: What is fragile-only packing?
answerFragments.text: What is fragile-only packing? Fragile-only packing covers the items where skill matters most: dishes and glassware, artwork and mirrors, TVs, lamps, china and crystal, antiques (1). They are packed with specialty materials and marked FRAGILE. In our scoping, fragile and high-value pieces escalate past the box when a box is not enough: a large mirror, a marble top, or an irreplaceable antique goes to white-glove handling or a custom-built crate. Name these pieces when the job is scoped — not on move day.

answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › Is packing included in a moving quote, or is it an add-on?
answerFragments.heading: Is packing included in a moving quote, or is it an add-on?
answerFragments.text: Is packing included in a moving quote, or is it an add-on? With most movers, packing is an add-on you must ask for: a standard moving quote covers loading and transport, and packing is priced separately when you request it (1). How it is priced varies — many companies bill packing by the hour, with minimum-hour requirements to send a crew out (1). Our model is different, and it is published: the packing level is scoped with the rest of the job — the items, the distance, the manpower, the equipment — and quoted inside the one flat rate in writing before move day. Packing is priced inside the one flat rate — there is no separate packing clock. Packing can also be booked on its own, without a move attached: packing only is one of the move types on our quote form.

answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › What will movers not pack?
answerFragments.heading: What will movers not pack?
answerFragments.text: What will movers not pack? Even on a full pack, some things a crew cannot take: hazardous materials — paint, solvents, propane, fuel — and perishables are the standard exclusions, and federal guidance is blunt that hazardous materials must never be hidden in household goods boxes (2). Plants travel badly and are usually excluded too. Irreplaceables — jewelry, documents, medication, cash — should travel with you, whoever packs the box (1).

answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › Does it matter who packs the box?
answerFragments.heading: Does it matter who packs the box?
answerFragments.text: Does it matter who packs the box? Yes, and it is the least-discussed part of the decision. Under the federal rules for interstate moves, a mover's liability can be reduced by your own acts — the FMCSA consumer booklet gives the example of improper packing of containers you pack yourself (2). If a box you packed arrives with the carton intact but the contents broken, fault is much harder to establish (1). The same booklet requires two liability options on interstate moves — full value protection, and released value at 60 cents per pound per article — and treats anything worth more than $100 per pound as an item of extraordinary value to declare in writing (2). The reading is simple: the more breakable and valuable the item, the stronger the case for having the crew pack it.

answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › How long does packing take?
answerFragments.heading: How long does packing take?
answerFragments.text: How long does packing take? It depends on the level and the density of the home. One Boston-area mover's published guide puts a full pack of a two-bedroom apartment at roughly four to six hours with a two-person crew, and a three-bedroom home with a basement and garage at six to ten (3). Read those as orientation, not a quote — your scope is set by a room-by-room review. The direction is certain: a room that takes a household a weekend takes a practiced crew a fraction of that, because packing is a system — right carton, right wrap, right label, in the right order. Level The crew packs You pack Chosen when Full packing Every room, every item class Nothing Time is short, the move is large, or the haul is long Partial packing The rooms you assign — usually the kitchen and fragile pieces Clothing, books, linens, the easy rooms You want the risk and the slow rooms off your plate Fragile-only packing Breakables and high-value pieces only Everything else The home is simple and the risk sits in a few items Example (illustrative): a Winchester household selling on a Friday closing chooses full packing. The crew scopes the job room by room the week before — kitchen, three bedrooms, home office, garage — and the written flat rate covers the pack and the move as one job. The owners keep out one suitcase of documents, medication and jewelry, which travels in their car.

answerFragments.locator: Do movers pack for you? › Frequently asked questions
answerFragments.heading: Frequently asked questions
answerFragments.text: Frequently asked questions Do movers pack for you, or do you have to pack yourself? Movers can pack for you — it is a standard service at three levels: full, partial, and fragile-only. You never have to pack yourself unless you prefer to. At The Flat Rate Movers, the level you choose is scoped room by room and quoted inside the one flat rate in writing before move day. Can I hire movers to pack only the kitchen? Yes. That is partial packing, and the kitchen is the most common single-room assignment because it holds the most breakables per shelf in the house. You name the rooms or item classes; the crew packs exactly those, labels them by room, and everything else in the home stays yours to pack. Is packing charged by the hour? At many companies, yes — packing is commonly billed hourly, sometimes with a minimum number of hours to send a crew (1). At The Flat Rate Movers it is not: packing is scoped with the job and priced inside the one flat rate in writing. No separate packing clock exists here. What should I pack myself, even with full packing? Keep the irreplaceables with you: jewelry, important documents, medication, cash, and anything you will need the first night. Movers cannot pack hazardous materials or perishables at any level (1, 2), so plan a separate route for paint, fuel, and propane. If I pack a box myself and something breaks, who is responsible? It is genuinely harder to claim. Federal consumer guidance notes that a mover's liability can be reduced by improper packing of containers you pack yourself (2), and if the carton arrives undamaged, fault is difficult to establish (1). That is the practical argument for fragile-only packing: the breakables are packed by the crew whose work stands behind them. Can I book packing without booking a move? Yes. Packing only is a bookable scope on our quote form — the crew packs the rooms you assign, and transport is yours to arrange separately. It is commonly used before a container load, a storage move-in, a freight shipment, or a self-managed long-distance move where you drive or ship the packed boxes yourself.

answerFragments.heading: What is partial packing?
answerFragments.text: What is partial packing? Partial packing is the middle level: you pack what you are comfortable packing — clothing, books, linens — and the crew packs the rooms or item classes you assign (1).
